mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals weakening household demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly below zero during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase of 0.4 percentage points or more signals tighter labor market conditions that raise wage pressures and inflation risk, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline of 3% or more in the industrial production index (INDPRO) signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of 2% or more in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a broad demand contraction, which reduces earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall > 2% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) increase of 0.75 percentage points or more within three months signals a tightening monetary cycle that raises discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous monthly decline of 0.3 percentage points or more in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and a rise of 0.5% in average hourly earnings (implied by labor market tightness) signals wage inflation risk, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls > 0.3pp and labor market tightness rises (implied by PAYEMS/UNRATE ratio)
regime_hint: tight labor market with wage pressure
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline of 1% or more in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over six consecutive months signals a persistent demand weakness that reduces earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during triggered episodes (t-test p > 0.05).
